$comment: Mission 1.70 §13 to §17. Documentation only. No index was queried and no WARC, WAT or WET file was downloaded.

crawl_identity.identifiers: crawls are named as dated releases, for example CC-MAIN-2026-34 and CC-MAIN-2016-30, and are addressed individually
crawl_identity.run_semantics: the identifier encodes a year and a release number; what the release period denotes was not stated on the pages read

immutability.$comment: §16. A date is not a guarantee.
immutability.what_is_established: a named crawl release is individually addressable, and past releases are listed alongside the current one
immutability.what_is_not_established: no retrieved page states that a released crawl or its index is retained unchanged, nor whether artifacts are append-only or may be replaced

url_selection.$comment: §14. Explicitly required by Mission 1.69, and NOT answered.
url_selection.what_was_read: the overview page, which carries no statement about seeds, the frontier, link discovery, sitemaps, popularity or ranking, whether previous crawls feed the next, or whether any target list is published before a crawl

a_search_summary_offered_an_answer_and_i.$comment: §45. Search summaries are navigation only, and this is the third mission in which one offered a load-bearing answer that no retrieved first-party page carried.
a_search_summary_offered_an_answer_and_i.what_the_summary_reported: a URL-prioritisation mechanism based on a graph-centrality measure, with seeds drawn within a small link distance of top-ranked hosts, and sitemap-derived additions
a_search_summary_offered_an_answer_and_i.why_it_was_not_used: no first-party page carrying that statement was opened, and §55 lists Common-Crawl-URL-selection-semantics-guessed among the things the validator must catch. Recording it as established would be exactly that.

coverage_semantics.$comment: §15 and §5. This is the load-bearing section.

source_says: status: the HTTP status code returned when fetching the page
digest: SHA-1 checksum of the contents of the capture
fetch_redirect: Target location of HTTP redirect
content_truncated: Non-null if the WARC record payload is truncated. The value indicates the reason for the truncation

coverage_semantics.project_interpretation: The index describes captures. Neither retrieved page states whether a URL that was fetched unsuccessfully, or attempted and never captured, appears at all. So presence in the index cannot be read as evidence of an ATTEMPT, and absence cannot be distinguished from never having been targeted.

metadata_value_boundary.why: The columnar index is Parquet, so a projection selecting only url and fetch_time is technically expressible without reading fetch_status.
metadata_value_boundary.and_why_that_does_not_settle_it: The technical boundary is navigable and the SEMANTIC one is not. Projecting a coverage list still yields a list whose meaning — attempted or captured — is undocumented, so the projection buys syntax rather than a population definition.

outcome_dependence.why: content_truncated records reasons including disconnect and time, which are fetch outcomes, and the index's own status field is an HTTP response code. Whether inclusion depends on the fetch succeeding is undocumented, so it cannot be ruled out.

http_semantics.robots_policy: an opt-out through robots.txt is documented
http_semantics.sitemaps: the crawler is documented as supporting the Sitemap Protocol
http_semantics.redirect_handling: a fetch_redirect field records the target of a redirect; whether a redirect response is itself captured as a record is not stated
http_semantics.timeouts_and_retries: a truncation reason of time implies a bound exists; no policy is documented
http_semantics.response_header_capture: the raw response including HTTP header information is stored in the WARC record

sampling.source_says: Common Crawl's dataset is a sample of the web, and we do not generally archive any entire website but a randomly selected subset of it.

route_status_reason: Its own fetching, raw response with headers, and dated individually addressed releases are established. What is not established is the coverage semantics, the URL selection mechanism and artifact immutability — none of which is a defect of the route and all of which a construct would have to name.
